# name <TAB> builder <TAB> source <TAB> flags
# `bash test/mkapp.sh --testing test/neutrinostdtheme.js test/neutrinostdtheme.cmd`
# appears in .github/workflows/ci.yml fifteen times, and it is one of eighty-four
# mkapp.sh lines across ten lanes. The artifact is the same artifact every time:
# the same source, the same flags, built on whichever runner needs it. Eighty-four
# lines saying twenty-five things is a file, not a workflow.
# `builder` is the column that made this a table rather than a column in
# suites.tsv. Almost everything here is mkapp.sh, but the app on the download
# page is not: test/demoapp.sh assembles pages/demo -- the four files that ship --
# with test/demoprobe.js concatenated onto the app's own script. A `build=` flag
# string could not have said that, and a directive per builder would have put the
# name of a program in the setup column of every row that used it.
# `source` is the .js mkapp.sh builds from, and it is here rather than derived
# because it is not always the name: neutrinostdgeom-none is neutrinostdgeom.js
# built with the decorations off, and a rule that derived the source from the
# name would have had no way to say so. `-` where the builder takes none.
# `flags` is passed through verbatim. `-` for none, which is not the same as
# `--testing` missing by accident: a release build and a testing build of one
# source are two rows here on purpose, because which one a lane runs is a fact
# about that lane and has been invisible in the YAML until now.
# Every artifact built here is passed through test/parse.sh before it runs. That
# was a per-step choice in fifty-four places and should never have been one: an
# artifact that does not parse is a suite that measures nothing, and finding out
# from the suite is finding out late.
